items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <b> tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies the purpose of the <u> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying underlined text.

rubric.why: Identifies the purpose of the tag.
rubric.description: States that displays or inserts an image in a webpage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an image.

modelAnswer: The <u> tag is used to underline text on a webpage.
The tag is used to insert or display an image on a webpage.

rubric.why: States the possible result of a logical expression.
rubric.description: Says that a logical expression evaluates to true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its possible values.

rubric.why: Identifies how a logical expression is formed.
rubric.description: Mentions a condition or the use of logical or relational operators.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its form or operators.

modelAnswer: A logical expression is a condition formed using variables, constants, and logical or relational operators.
When evaluated, it gives a result of either true or false.

rubric.why: Shows the correct grouping method for binary-to-hexadecimal conversion.
rubric.description: Groups the binary digits into sets of four, starting from the right; pads the leftmost group with zeros if needed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining or showing groups of four.
Award 1 mark for the correct hexadecimal answer.

modelAnswer: Group the binary digits into sets of four from the right: (0100 0001)₂.
Convert each group to its hexadecimal digit: 0100 = 4 and 0001 = 1.

rubric.why: Rewards correct place-value expansion of the binary number.
rubric.description: Shows the powers-of-two expansion for the non-zero binary digits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct expansion or equivalent place-value calculation.
Award 1 mark for the correct answer.

rubric.why: Identifies that softlifting involves unauthorized copying.
rubric.description: States that softlifting is unauthorized or illegal copying of software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unauthorized copying.

rubric.why: Explains the license violation involved in softlifting.
rubric.description: Mentions installing or using licensed software on more computers or by more users than the license allows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying use beyond the license terms.

modelAnswer: Softlifting is the unauthorized copying or installation of licensed software.
It occurs when software is used on more computers or by more users than permitted by its license.

items.followUp: What is a server in a client-server network?

rubric.why: Explains the client's role in the model.
rubric.description: States that a client requests data or a service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the client request.

rubric.why: Explains the server's role in the model.
rubric.description: States that the server provides the requested data or service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the server response or service.

modelAnswer: In a client-server network, a client is a computer or user that requests data or a service.
A server is a computer that receives the request and provides the requested data or service.

items.followUp: Give one example of hardware that can be shared on a network.

rubric.description: States that hardware sharing makes a physical device available to multiple network users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing access to a shared device by users.

rubric.why: Provides a relevant example of shared hardware.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as a printer or storage device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable hardware example.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing allows multiple users on a network to use the same hardware device.
For example, several users can share a network printer.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a client and a server in a network.

rubric.why: Identifies the function of a client.
rubric.description: States that a client requests data or a service from a network computer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the client’s role.

rubric.why: Identifies the function of a server.
rubric.description: States that a server provides data or services to clients.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the server’s role.

modelAnswer: A client is a computer that requests data or services from another computer on a network.
A server is a computer that provides data or services to client computers.
